sections.h2: How can a Carrollton homeowner sell, and which route is quickest?
sections.html:
Three routes exist in Carrollton: hire an agent, sell privately, or hand the house to a cash buyer who takes it as it stands. The right one depends on the house's condition, the calendar, and whether tenants or co-owners complicate matters.

  • Agent listing: the biggest pool of buyers, with showings, inspection requests and a lender's schedule.
  • Private sale: no listing agent, but pricing and paperwork fall to you.
  • Cash purchase as-is: fewer steps and no repair demands, at a price normally under a polished listing.

Renters outnumber owners in Carrollton. The Census Bureau puts the homeownership rate at 41.0 percent for 2020-2024, and 73.9 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, so turnover in the housing stock is steady.

sections.h2: How did the University of West Georgia grow out of Carrollton?
sections.html:
The University of West Georgia occupies the western side of Carrollton, and its story starts in the city. A 1906 state law created agricultural and mechanical schools for each congressional district. In 1907, trustees bought the 275-acre Bluford Sharp farm west of town for $9,625 as the Fourth District A&M School site, and classes began in January 1908.

After the Board of Regents picked the Carrollton campus on April 15, 1933, it became West Georgia College. It turned into the State University of West Georgia in 1996 and the University of West Georgia on January 12, 2005, according to the university library's timeline. A small reminder of the town-campus link: the campus chapel was built in 1893 in downtown Carrollton and moved to the grounds in 1964.

Not every street feels the campus, so ask a local agent or investor how far your house is from it before assuming student demand reaches your block.

sections.h2: How does Carrollton compare with the country on housing and income?
sections.html:
QuickFacts estimates 27,925 people for mid-2025, 4.5 percent above the April 2020 estimates base, spread across 22.41 square miles of land. Measures below cover 2020-2024.

Figures come from the Census tables for Carrollton and the United States. House values sit a little under the national midpoint, while incomes and rents sit well under it. Owners with a mortgage pay a midpoint $1,590 monthly, against $1,963 nationally, and 88.5 percent of households subscribe to broadband. With poverty at 25.4 percent, affordability limits many local buyers, and a house needing work may lose more value in a retail sale than the repair would cost.

Other Census entries: 35.2 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree, 9.1 percent of residents were born abroad, and 2022 retail sales came to $34,866 per resident, above the $20,928 national figure, which points to a shopping and service hub for the surrounding area.

sections.h2: Which public schools serve Carrollton houses?
sections.html:
Carrollton City Schools operates its own district, which describes four schools on a single 130-acre campus: Carrollton Elementary, Carrollton Upper Elementary, Carrollton Middle School and Carrollton High. The district office is at 106 Trojan Drive.

Whether a given address falls inside that district depends on the city limits, so confirm the district with the school system before you state it in a listing. Parents often ask about schools first, and a correct answer helps a serious buyer move faster.

sections.h2: What does Carrollton require for short-term rentals?
sections.html:
Carrollton added a short-term rental article to its code in July 2025, as Chapter 18, Article VI. The code defines a short-term rental as a dwelling, or part of one, rented for lodging for 30 consecutive days or fewer, and no one may rent without a license.

  • The license is annual, with a non-refundable $500 application fee filed with Community Development.
  • Occupancy tops out at two adults per bedroom, with one vehicle per bedroom parked on paved surfaces, never on the street.
  • External signs are banned, and the license number must appear on every online listing.
  • Three convictions or judgments for code violations trigger a 12-month revocation.
  • Appeals of a denial, suspension or revocation go in writing to the Mayor and City Council within 30 calendar days.

Hotel-motel tax applies as well. A license belongs to one owner and one address and cannot be transferred, so a buyer who intends a rental needs a new license. The city's licensing and permit office answers questions at 770-830-2000.

sections.h2: How do Carroll County assessments and tax bills affect a Carrollton sale?
sections.html:
Carroll County values and bills Carrollton property. Its tax page explains that assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value as of January 1, and that one mill equals $1.00 per $1,000 of assessed value. Several bodies set rates: county commissioners for county operations, the board of education for schools, and the state, which may levy no more than a quarter of a mill.

Value disputes go first to the Board of Tax Assessors and then, if needed, to the County Board of Equalization, appointed by the grand jury. A taxpayer may pick arbitration in its place when filing. Georgia assessment notices carry a 45-day appeal window, so rely on the date printed on yours. In Carroll County, returns and homestead applications run through the Board of Assessors, while the tax commissioner prepares bills and collects: call 770-830-5843 about calculations, late payments and interest.

A transfer tax applies to the sale too. State revenue guidance gives the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents per further $100 or part of $100, charged to the seller unless the contract moves it to the buyer. For questions about exemptions, ask the Carroll County clerk of superior court.

faqs.q: Do most Carrollton households own their homes?
faqs.a: No. The Census Bureau lists the homeownership rate at 41.0 percent for 2020-2024, compared with 65.2 percent nationally, so most households rent.

faqs.q: How many people live in Carrollton, GA?
faqs.a: About 27,900. The mid-2025 estimate is 27,925, against 26,738 in the 2020 census and 24,388 in 2010.

faqs.q: Do Airbnb-style rentals need a license in Carrollton?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires an annual license, with a $500 non-refundable application fee, for stays of 30 consecutive days or fewer. The license does not transfer to a new owner.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill for a Carrollton house?
faqs.a: Carroll County. The Board of Tax Assessors sets values, and the county tax commissioner prepares and mails bills, collects payment and takes questions at 770-830-5843.

faqs.q: Can a Carrollton house with tenants be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer paying cash and accepting the house as-is can take it subject to the lease. Disclose the lease terms early and ask whoever runs your closing how deposits and rent are handled.
